name: China
no_index_reason: No index is published for this country. The Monitored-Area ESDI's sector weights, decay horizons and transmission measure were built for a strike campaign and do not transfer (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §1-§3). This view shows reported major disruptions and energy-system context instead.

sectors.reason: No complete single-basis refinery registry exists in open data; the independent and large private refiners are covered only by commercial databases.
sectors.label: Refining

sectors.reason: Becomes EXPERIMENTAL only once GEM's unit-level power tracker is acquired; capacity grew 16% in 2025, so a frozen denominator would be a first-order error. Not scored. The recovery and decay model behind the Monitored-Area ESDI was calibrated on repeated strikes with almost no restart reporting, and no model for this country's events has been approved (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §2 and §8.3).
sectors.label: Electric generation

reporting_environment_text: Operators and authorities do not publish event-level outage reports. Events come from media and company statements, so most smaller disruptions will not appear.
reporting_note: Event-level outage reports are not published by operators or regulators. Accident reporting centres on casualties and accountability, not output, and much of it is in Chinese only.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: 31 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities, plus Hong Kong and Macau as special administrative regions, and the Paracel Islands as drawn by Natural Earth. Boundaries show the line of actual control (Natural Earth's default edition), which is an analytic choice, not a statement about sovereignty. Taiwan is not part of this system.

rulings.note: Contains Aksai Chin, administered by China and claimed by India.
Borders Arunachal Pradesh, which China claims and India administers; that territory is drawn with India.
Paracel Islands: administered by China, claimed by Vietnam and Taiwan. Drawn; never assigned an event.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.single_statement: One source statement reported these records together.
episode_bases.continuing_shortfall: A later record reports the same supply shortfall continuing.
episode_bases.single_record: No other record is tied to this one by name or source.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-10-30 by the China source-audit lane. CONTEXT ONLY, never a scoring input. NBS 2025 figures are preliminary (Communique note 1) and whole-economy scope; NBS monthly releases cover only industrial enterprises above designated size and differ in level (2025 electricity: 9,715.9 vs 10,575.25 billion kWh) - never mix the two scopes. Mainland China only (31 provincial-level units); excludes Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. See docs/countries/CN_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

significance: EIA describes China as the world's top coal producer and consumer (2023 production 4.8 billion short tons).
China's total primary energy output was 5.13 billion tonnes of standard coal equivalent in 2025 (NBS, preliminary).
China's installed generating capacity reached 3,891.34 GW at end-2025, including 1,201.73 GW of solar and 640.01 GW of wind (NBS).
EIA reports China was the top global natural gas importer in 2023, with LNG 61% of imports.

research_gaps: Not yet researched: East China industrial power curbs (Aug 2022), winter gas shortages, power-plant outages, and restoration dates for the Sichuan and Chongqing curbs.
Several typhoon outages have no readable sourced customer count and are held as insufficient evidence rather than inferred: Saola (2023), Kajiki (2025, Hainan) and Noul (2026, Guangdong).

onboarding_gate.label: Threshold declared; every event carries its basis, criterion and episode
onboarding_gate.note: Threshold, inclusion basis, criterion and episode on every event. Episodes are curated by hand under a stated rule, and counts are given in both records and episodes.

onboarding_gate.label: Safety tests extended to the country
onboarding_gate.note: The served-data gates recurse into every country payload.

onboarding_gate.label: Freshness: last refresh per source, with a stale notice
onboarding_gate.note: Every source states when it was last checked and how long it stays fresh, and the page marks any source past that limit. The event search itself has not covered the whole window: at least one research pass ended with its budget spent, so recent years are under-searched.

onboarding_gate.label: Comparability fields and structural rules
onboarding_gate.note: comparability 'none', reporting environment on every count, fixed alphabetical order, no shared scale.
